title: Seatless capacity buffer, graduated ops-response ladders, and rolling upgrade policy for Private/VPC deployments
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Enterprise customers buying Private/VPC deployments want predictable billing and operational SLAs without the overhead of per-seat licenses. Current options either require large committed GPU/seat blocks or ad-hoc premium support add-ons that are hard to compare across deals. We need a pricing and entitlement construct that: 1) smooths monthly/quarterly usage spikes (seatless capacity buffer), 2) defines clear ops-response ladders (self-serve / standard / premium / enterprise) tied to measurable SLAs and Escalation Paths, and 3) adds a rolling upgrade cadence for on-prem customers that balances security patching with customer change windows. This ticket experiments with a blended commercial proposal and a small set of pilot customers to validate economics and contract language.
proposal_summary: Introduce a 'Capacity Buffer' credit model (monthly pool of commit credits consumable by any node in the tenancy) sized at 10-30% of baseline committed throughput; define three Ops Ladders (Standard: 24x7 chat + 72h P1, Priority: 24x7 phone + 24h P1, Critical: named escalation + 4h P1) with explicit pricing uplift bands; and publish a Rolling Upgrade Policy: quarterly security patches mandatory with opt-out windows and annual minor upgrade windows. Offer a pilot pricing sheet with two variants: 'Buffer Lite' (10% buffer, Standard ladder) and 'Buffer Plus' (25% buffer, Priority ladder + monthly health check).
acceptance_criteria: Legal-approved contract clause for capacity buffer and credit reconciliation
Three pilot quotes produced and shared with sales engineering
Billing prototype that can reconcile buffer consumption to invoices and show buffer depletion alerts in Console
Support runbook with defined SLAs and on-call escalation ladder published
Security team sign-off on rolling upgrade cadence and opt-out controls

decision: Run a 12-week pilot with two current customers and one prospect: deploy Buffer Plus to one customer, Buffer Lite to another, and offer an opt-in trial to the prospect. If pilot shows <8% average buffer waste and no more than two SLA escalations, proceed to formalize pricing bands and add to standard private deployment SKUs.
